subject: Benchmark methodology + reproducibility asks for FastRetail SLO qualification
messages:
From: Sophie Lemaire <sophie.lemaire@fastretail.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 14:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — performance targets and benchmark approach

Hi team,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a request for your benchmark methodology so we can qualify FastRetail against our internal SLOs. High-level asks below — please send the minimal artifacts so our infra team can reproduce a run.

Key SLOs we care about:
- P95 latency <= 120 ms for single-turn product search generation (median sequence length ~64 tokens)
- Sustained throughput of 180 QPS at 250 concurrent connections for our peak region (eu-west)
- Streaming support: we need chunked responses with max chunk latency 40 ms and useful partial tokens emitted every ~60 ms when streaming to the browser

What we need from Redwood to reproduce qualification:
1) Prompt set and token accounting (CSV or JSONL) that maps to our 4 main query archetypes
2) Measurement definitions: how you compute P95/P99, warmup handling, KV cache priming, and sampling method for concurrency
3) Harness instructions: container/instance types, open-source harness (if any), and command-line steps to replay the workload
4) Test data: we can share a small sample set; prefer an initial run with 1k queries so we can sanity-check numbers

Ops notes:
- We'll run in our eu-west region; please confirm any model variants or quantization profiles you recommend for cost/latency balance.
- Procurement will need an official run result and an IP/data handling note for proof.

Can you share a short packet (prompt set + harness guide + measurement defs) by Tuesday so we can line up a run later that week?

Thanks,
Sophie
--
Sophie Lemaire
Head of Engineering, FastRetail
Sophie.Lemaire@fastretail.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 17:34:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — performance targets and benchmark approach

Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Attached is an initial packet to get the reproduction started. I kept the artifacts intentionally minimal so your infra team can run without a deep Redwood setup.

Attachments included:
- prompt_set_v1.csv (CSV): 200 representative queries across your 4 archetypes with expected token counts and the small prompt templates we used in the demo
- harness_instructions.md (MD): step-by-step harness run using our open harness (Docker + k6 wrapper) plus example CLI commands
- measurement_definitions.md (MD): definitions for p95/p99, warmup windows, concurrency semantics, and how we handle streaming chunk latency

Short answers to your bullets:
- Model recommendations: for eu-west and the latency target you quoted, we suggest the quantized-medium variant (q6_K32) for initial runs. It gives a good latency/cost balance and supports streaming.
- KV cache priming: our harness primes cache per-shard using a sampled set; measurement_definitions.md includes the exact sequence for deterministic priming.
- Warmup: default 3 minutes or 10k tokens, whichever comes first; you can override based on your traffic profile.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm if your infra team can run Docker images and provide an internal test node or allow outbound test to our private harness endpoint.
2) If you prefer, we can run the first pass from Redwood in a shared test region and provide the raw harness logs.

We'll be available Tuesday for a run or to walk through the artifacts — propose 09:00 - 12:00 CEST.

Best,
Priyom
Priyom Das

Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:11:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — performance targets and benchmark approach

Sophie — quick technical clarifications from my side so we measure apples-to-apples:

1) Tokenization: the prompt_set_v1.csv includes columns for prompt_tokens and response_token_est; please confirm if your client-side pretokenization matches our tokenizer (we included a small script in harness_instructions.md to verify).

2) Concurrency semantics: when you say 250 concurrent connections, do you mean 250 long-lived websocket streams (streaming responses) or 250 simultaneous short-lived HTTP requests? The behavior and batching implications differ.

3) Latency measurement: our measurement_definitions.md reports server-side end-to-end token emission latencies for streaming (chunk emit time) and request-complete latency for non-streaming. For your UI, which metric matters more? p95 of complete response or p95 of first-chunk/partial tokens?

Suggested defaults for the first run to match your ask:
- Treat 250 as websocket-style long-lived streams sending 1 request at a time; concurrency will be simulated via 250 parallel connections in the harness.
- Report both: first-chunk p50/p95 and full-response p50/p95/p99.
- Include CPU/GPU utilization and per-shard request distribution in the run logs.

Finally, for reproducibility: we recommend recording the model seed, quantization profile, and kernel selection used during each run. measurement_definitions.md has fields for each.

Happy to join the run on Tuesday to help interpret results.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
